messages:
pagerbot: [ALERT] GPU pool 'us-west-2/gpu-hot-1' saturation; queue length spike (qps->throttle) detected for model 'rw-l2-7b' at 2026-03-31T02:09:03Z. Autoscaler attempted scale but hit hard cap (max_shards=12). Pager level: sev2. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-saturation
elaine: ack — I'm oncall. grabbing metrics now. Anyone on infra side? :hand:
sam: I'm here. I see queue growth starting ~02:02Z. qlen went from ~120 -> 2.1k in 6m. GPU utils 98%. Autoscaler logs show repeated "max_shards_reached" and "scale_backoff".
devon: adding logs snippet: ```2026-03-31T02:07:41Z autoscaler: scale_attempt key=gpu-hot-1 target=14 result=max_shards_reached
2026-03-31T02:08:12Z batcher: prefix_cache_miss_rate=0.47, continuous_batch_drop=0.23
2026-03-31T02:08:44Z runtime: throttling requests=312, errors=5
```
maria: that's a big prefix miss spike — unusual. Any recent deploys touching batching/cache params?
elaine: yes — yesterday's runtime rollout (canary) included change: continuous_batch.window_ms from 50 -> 200 and prefix_cache.eviction_policy switched to lfu_ttl=30s -> lru_ttl=5s. I asked for a followup test but it was merged.
sam: that matches the timeline. Increased batch window + aggressive prefix eviction = worse effective batching for many short-chat requests -> more tokens, longer per-request runtime and less cache hits. Autoscaler sees higher per-request token work and hits shard cap.
oncall-ops: customer-ops reporting elevated 429s and increased latency. Top-tier customers: AcmeCorp and NovaChat seeing errors in region us-west-2. Support ticket numbers: #INC-49319, #INC-49321.
customer-ops: AcmeCorp says TTL-sensitive inference jobs time out; NovaChat reported "server busy" spikes 02:10-02:15Z. Estimated % of their requests throttled ~12-18%.
devon: quick mitigation options (ranked):
1) revert runtime rollout that changed batching/prefix policy (risky but targeted).
2) temporarily raise autoscaler hard cap for this pool (requires infra approval).
3) route heavy customers to smaller model variant rw-l2-7b-lite (lower perf) until pool recovers.
4) reduce continuous_batch.window_ms back to previous value via dynamic flag.

sam: infra says we can lift `max_shards` for 30m as emergency. I can run that if we decide.
elaine: let's do a two-pronged approach: (A) lift max_shards to 18 now; (B) revert continuous_batch.window_ms to 50ms in the runtime config for canary+prod to stop further degradation. Apply (A) first to buy time.
oncall-ops: agree. Prioritize customer-facing fix.
elaine: @sam please run scale now and @devon please prepare a rollback PR for the runtime flag and a hotfix rollout. Also open a canary hold so the rest of rollout doesn't proceed.
sam: running: ```kubectl -n inference patch cm gpu-autoscaler-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"max_shards":"18"}}'```
sam: infra confirms API responded OK. Autoscaler target cap now 18. Watching queue.
ops-bot: [AUDIT] Config change applied by sam at 2026-03-31T02:13:12Z: max_shards 12 -> 18 (ticket: CHG-1102).
devon: rollback PR opened: https://git.redwood/runtime/pulls/4123 — reverting continuous_batch.window_ms and prefix_cache.eviction_policy. Will wait approval then hotpatch.
maria: monitoring: prefix_cache_miss_rate fell from 0.47 -> 0.21 within 90s after cap increase (likely due to reduced backpressure causing some caches to warm). Queue length dropping from 2.1k -> 600. GPU util still high ~92% but trending down.
elaine: good. Meanwhile, start routing AcmeCorp and NovaChat to rw-l2-7b-lite via feature-flagged route. @customer-ops can you coordinate with them?
customer-ops: pinged both customers, applying route override now. Will monitor for error count drop.
ops-bot: [ROUTE] Traffic override applied for AcmeCorp -> rw-l2-7b-lite by customer-ops at 2026-03-31T02:15:03Z.
maria: after routes + cap increase, error rate for AcmeCorp dropped from 14% -> 3% in first 2 minutes. NovaChat from 12% -> 2.5%. Latency p95 reduced ~400ms.
sam: can we add an emergency metric alarm for prefix_cache_miss_rate > 0.2? Right now it was 0.47 and that correlates strongly with impact.
devon: yes we should. I'll file a followup alert and add a dashboard annotation to correlate batch_window and prefix misses. PR will include recommended guardrails to block batch window changes without a perf validation.
elaine: on-call handoff note: I'll hold for 20m to verify rollback and customer stabilization, then hand to devon for postmortem. Key followups: why did runtime change land without validation? add pre-release perf test (synthetic short-chat load), add autoscaler soft throttle signal to trigger config rollback or routing earlier.
oncall-ops: I'll create incident ticket INC-49345 with timeline, customer impact, and mitigation steps. Assign to devon for RCA.
pagerbot: [RESOLVE PREDICTION] Queue trending to normal; incident status will be updated to resolved if metrics stable for 30m.
elaine: thanks all. small ask for charges: record any cost delta from raising cap. @sam please note instance spin-up cost.
sam: noted. Spun up 6 extra nodes for ~18m. Estimate $1.9k additional for this window (prelim).
devon: capturing timeline and will run RCA. Preliminary root cause: batching window increase + aggressive prefix eviction change combined -> increased per-request work, reduced cache reuse -> autoscaler hit hard cap -> queue growth -> customer throttles. We'll propose guardrails and preflight tests in the postmortem.
customer-ops: customers updated and will follow-up if anything else. Closing high-touch alerts for AcmeCorp after confirmation.
elaine: handing off now to devon for postmortem and action items. Staying reachable if anything flips. :white_check_mark:
devon: taking over. I'll post a full postmortem draft within 24 hours. tagging runbook owner @maria to update the rollout checklist.
ops-bot: [INCIDENT] INC-49345 created by oncall-ops at 2026-03-31T02:22:30Z (severity: sev2)"
